episode_title: What Do AI Agents and AI Platforms Think Your Business Does? | Ep.290
question: How can AI platforms like ChatGPT misunderstand what your business actually does today?
transcript_excerpt: AI platforms learn about your business from publicly available information like your website, content, and business profiles. If that information is outdated, incomplete, or inconsistent, they can end up with the wrong picture of what your business actually does. They might miss a new service you're trying to grow, misunderstand the type of customers you want to work with, or keep associating your company with something you stopped doing years ago.

podcast_name: AI Visibility for Business Owners & Marketing Teams | bcjr Podcast
episode_title: What Do AI Agents and AI Platforms Think Your Business Does? | Ep.290
question: What three basic questions should you ask AI platforms to test whether they understand your company correctly?
transcript_excerpt: Start with three basic questions: What does this company do? What does this company specialize in? And who does this company appear to serve? Then make the questions more specific to the business. If you're local, include your market or service area. If you're B2B, ask about the capability or type of customer that matters most to you.

podcast_name: AI Visibility for Business Owners & Marketing Teams | bcjr Podcast
episode_title: What Do AI Agents and AI Platforms Think Your Business Does? | Ep.290
question: Why is incomplete information about your business more significant than factually wrong information in AI-generated answers?
transcript_excerpt: While factually wrong information needs attention, incomplete information can be even more interesting. For example, if a roofing company does both residential and commercial roofing but AI platforms almost always describe it as residential roofing, that's technically not wrong but it's not the whole company and misrepresents all the services offered. If commercial roofing is an important part of where the business is going, that missing piece matters even more.

episode_title: What Do AI Agents and AI Platforms Think Your Business Does? | Ep.290
question: How should you use podcast content to improve AI visibility and understanding of your business?
transcript_excerpt: Create multiple podcast episodes with educational content that explains in detail the problem and solution. Then turn the podcast episode into a page on your website that includes the entire episode transcript and is structured for both humans and machines to read and understand. By doing this consistently, you're not just claiming expertise on a service page—you're putting useful information behind it, based on something you know from experience and something you've actually gotten results from.

podcast_name: AI Visibility for Business Owners & Marketing Teams | bcjr Podcast
episode_title: What Do AI Agents and AI Platforms Think Your Business Does? | Ep.290
question: What should you do after you've updated your business information online to verify AI platforms have recognized the changes?
transcript_excerpt: Go back later and run the same questions again. Not because you expect every answer to suddenly change, but because you want to see whether the picture starts getting more accurate over time. The progress you should be looking for is whether AI platforms and AI agents have enough clear information to discover your business, understand what you actually do, and trust the information enough to potentially recommend you when you're relevant.
